prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE botanical game-asset reference of a juvenile bok choy / Brassica rapa Chinensis Group plant at the middle growth stage. Image 1 defines the approved gongbi fine-line/light-colour style; image 2 is actual young plants for anatomy, focus on the individual small bok choy in foreground, NOT the frilly lettuces in the background. Single loose open rosette of FIVE true leaves: three larger obovate/spoon-shaped green leaves on slim broadening ivory-to-pale-green petioles, two smaller upright central leaves. An optional tiny fading cotyledon at base only. Petioles modestly widened at base, each visibly distinct, not the thick swollen white mature bundle. Outer leaves spread diagonally upward and outward, inner leaves rise; all leaf blades stay ABOVE the small unified planting base. No hanging leaves below root collar. All petioles join naturally, no detached fragments or exposed roots. A genuinely juvenile independent structure, fewer/smaller leaves than mature and no compact cabbage head. Elevated three-quarter camera looking down 35 degrees, round radial footprint with clear near, far and lateral leaf depth, not flat fan. Thin gently curved blades, smooth slightly undulating margins, prominent pale midrib and fine selected branching veins, fresh muted sage/celadon watercolor wash and mottling with visible organized gongbi outlines. No inflated rubber forms, glossy plastic, yellow antique filter or neon green. Plain light-gray neutral background, diffuse even light, no ground, soil, pot, shadow, labels, text, or extra objects. Whole silhouette inside frame. Emphasize traceable leaf-to-petiole-to-base connections suitable for 3D reconstruction.
review: Revised narrower juvenile petioles with near/far leaf overlap and radial depth; no swollen mature base.
revision_prompt: Correct this juvenile bok choy reference for 3D reconstruction. Keep its muted sage gongbi fine outlines and pigment washes, species and five true leaves, but CHANGE its anatomy and camera. The existing white petioles are too thick and look mature: reduce their width by about 60 percent, leave visible air gaps between all five thin spoon-shaped petioles, no swollen bulb or onion-like base. The bottom is a tiny narrow joined crown ending at the planting line. Remove the two tiny floppy leaves at the base. Make the five leaves grow in a ROUND radial rosette with near, far, left, right, and center positions, not a flat five-finger fan. Camera looks steeply DOWN at 50 degrees: the foreground leaf visibly projects toward the viewer, broad surface strongly foreshortened and its lower edge curved upward; rear leaf partly obscured behind upright central leaf; lateral leaf turned partly edge-on. Allow intentional overlap and view-dependent foreshortening: do not turn every leaf face toward camera. This should look like a small dimensional 3D hand-painted plant photographed from above, with oval tops and spatial gaps, not a flat botanical diagram. Slender young ivory/pale-green stalks connect smoothly to the blades and converge at the same base. Soft neutral volumetric shading, matte thin leaves with readable contours and pale main veins. Whole plant in frame, no roots, soil, pot, ground disk, typography or extra objects. Plain neutral-gray backdrop.
